name: MailTester Ninja Email Verification and Finder API
description:
One GET request per address. MailTester Ninja checks the address against the recipient's live mail server (syntax, domain, MX records, then an SMTP conversation that stops before any message is sent) and returns a verdict. Nothing is stored.

Branch your code on `code`:

| code | Meaning | Typical `message` |
|------|---------|-------------------|
| `ok` | Valid and deliverable | Accepted |
| `ko` | Invalid, will bounce | Rejected, No MX, Disposable, Limited |
| `mb` | Uncertain: the domain accepts everything or could not be probed | Catch-All, MX Error, Timeout, SPAM Block, Greylisted, Abuse |
| `--` | No verdict, the address was not checked | Invalid Key, Disabled Key, free limit message (HTTP 429) |

A catch-all domain is never reported as valid. Never drop an address on a `--` answer: fix the key, or wait and retry.

**Keys and limits.** Pass `key=free` to try the API with no signup (10 checks a day per IP), a free token `mtf_...` from https://mailtester.ninja/free-email-verification-api/ (50 checks a day, valid 7 days), or a subscription key `sub_...` from https://mailtester.ninja/verify-emails-unlimited/. The free tier allows one request every 30 seconds. A paid key allows its daily limit divided by 8640 requests per 10 seconds, for all connections together (Pro 11, Ultimate 23 per 10 seconds; buy a quantity to multiply it).

**Finder API.** `GET /find` takes `first`, `last` and `domain` and tests the most common address formats one by one (first.last, flast, first, firstlast, first_last, f.last) until the mail server accepts one. It stops early when the answer applies to the whole domain: on a catch-all domain the most common format is returned as `guess`. Personal email providers such as gmail.com are not searched. Paid keys only. Each format tested counts as one verification against the daily limit and the rate of the key, even when nothing is found; the `/find` call itself is not counted. The search paces its formats within the rate of the key; if the key is already at its maximum, it answers HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header. One key can run up to 60 searches an hour on the same domain.

**Content type.** On `/ninja`, send `Accept: application/json` to receive `application/json`; without it the same JSON body is served as `text/plain`. `/find` always answers `application/json`.

Code examples for cURL, Python, Node.js, PHP, Go, Ruby, Java, C#, Google Sheets, n8n, Make, Zapier, Clay and AI agents: https://mailtester.ninja/integrations/code-examples/ (also on GitHub: https://github.com/mailtester-ninja/mailtester-api-examples)
